Hi Elena / SolSupply team,

Thanks again for choosing Redwood. We're excited to get your account set up so we can start routing purchase orders and finalize the first POs for Q3. A couple of issues popped up during the self-serve Ariba registration that we want to address together:

1) Account collision: your Ariba sign-up reports an existing seller record associated with the same tax ID/email. That prevents a new account from being created and is blocking PO acceptance testing. Please see attached screenshot (ariba_sso_error.png).

2) KYC & onboarding checklist: to complete our vendor record we need the items below. I've attached a spreadsheet checklist (vendor_onboarding_checklist.xlsx) to track progress. If you can return the docs via email or upload to the Drive link below, we'll process the vendor setup:
- Completed W9 (or local tax form) (attached: solsupply_W9.pdf if available)
- Company legal name and DBA
- Tax ID / VAT number / DUNS (if available)
- Remittance address and preferred payment method (ACH details OR purchase card contact)
- Primary PO acceptance email and accounts-payable contact
- Copy of SOC2/ISO certificate or statement of processing if available (optional)

Next steps I propose:
- Elena: confirm whether SolSupply already has a legacy Ariba seller ID and share that ID if available.
- Laura (ops): once we have the seller ID, can you validate with our Ariba admin whether we can link / merge the records or whitelist the new account attempt?
- Neha (procurement): can you review the checklist and flag any additional vendor requirements for payments > $50k?

Drive checklist: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3-onboarding-checklists
HubSpot company: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/7890

Happy to hop on a 20-min call to walk through the steps if that helps. Availability: today 2–4pm PT or tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Procurement Ops Manager

Thanks Marcus — I checked with Teresa (Ariba admin). Short summary:
- If SolSupply provides the legacy seller ID we can request a merge. Merges require a ticket to the Ariba support portal and typically take 3–5 business days.
- There's an internal safety check: if the legacy seller has an open PO with invoiced items, Ariba will not auto-merge; manual reconciliation required.
- If SolSupply prefers, we can provision a new seller ID on our side and set the PO acceptance email to the new account to avoid disrupting legacy flows. That route is faster (1–2 business days) but may leave duplicate records that we'd need to reconcile later.

Action items:
- Marcus: confirm whether SolSupply's finance is comfortable with a temporary new seller provisioning (faster) or wants us to pursue a merge (slower but cleaner).
- Neha: I'll add a note to the vendor record to guard against duplicate invoice processing; we'll also set a tag "manual-reconcile" until we complete the reconciliation.

I'll start the Ariba support ticket if Elena confirms legacy ID.

Laura Bennett
Procurement Systems Lead
Redwood Inference
